name: Intel Gaudi 3 accelerators via OEM partners (Dell, HPE, Supermicro)
region: Worldwide via Dell, HPE and Supermicro storefronts
notes: QUOTE-ONLY. Intel's Gaudi product page carries a 'Shop' section that does NOT sell Gaudi directly - it links out to three OEM storefronts: Dell (dell.com/en-us/lp/intel-xeon), HPE (buy.hpe.com ProLiant compute) and Supermicro (supermicro.com/en/accelerators/intel). That is the whole enterprise purchase path for Gaudi 3, and it is why this record is filed as an integrator channel rather than an OEM-direct one. Note the Intel storefront URL is the generic Xeon landing page, which is itself evidence of how thin Gaudi volume is: there is no dedicated Gaudi buying surface, only a badge on the Xeon page. SKUs: HL-338 PCIe add-in card, HL-325L OAM mezzanine card, and HLB-325 universal baseboard - the UBB is the 8-accelerator baseboard, so as with SXM/HGX the multi-GPU unit is the board, not a separable module. Intel does publish product briefs for HL-338 and HLB-325 but no prices. Cloud alternatives (IBM Cloud, AWS EC2 DL1, Denvr) are the other common way to reach Gaudi capacity. EXPORT CONTROLLED (true). Regime: US BIS advanced-computing export controls (the Oct 2023 interim final rule, 88 FR 73458 - source sup-buy-bis-2023-advanced-computing-controls), which put datacenter accelerators under ECCN 3A090/4A090, added the advanced-computing Foreign Direct Product (FDP) rule, and extended Regional Stability (RS) controls to Country Groups D:1, D:4 and D:5. For items destined to Macau or Country Group D:5 the rule applies a PRESUMPTION OF DENIAL; other RS destinations get a presumption of approval. Practical effect: which accelerator you can legally be sold, and which SKU counts as compliant, is set by destination and end user - not by the channel.
